BFM and BVR Practice

Virtual Egyptian Air Force · 2026-10-28 · AI-assisted debrief · approved by Sword
TRAININGBFMBVRA-A

Instructor narrative

The Sinai training mission ran from 02:11 to approximately 03:01, encompassing five BFM rounds and five A-A/BVR rounds across all four pilots. In BFM, [EAF] MeGaTron dominated comprehensively: he defeated [EAF] PushMaster in Rounds 1 and 4/5, and Golden_Pilot in Round 3, converting neutral positions to gun saddle via superior energy management in the turning fight. PushMaster was consistently unable to hold an offensive position against MeGaTron — 0% offensive time in Round 1, 19% in Round 4 despite firing 423 rounds for zero hits, a clear indication that he is pulling the trigger from outside a valid firing solution. Both BFM pilots committed multiple deck busts (MeGaTron 2–3 per slot, PushMaster 2 per slot) and racked up sustained over-G events that are the primary safety concern of this debrief. The transition to BVR at Round 6 reshuffled the hierarchy: Golden_Pilot emerged as the session's most lethal pilot with 5 kills, including tight-parameter shots at 2.1–9.8 nm. PushMaster found his form in BVR, scoring 4 kills with patient, close-range employment. MeGaTron struggled in BVR, going 1-for-3 in kills while dying repeatedly — his BFM instinct to close to guns does not translate well when he needs to manage radar picture and employ BVR missiles at optimal range. ToRnAdO joined the BVR fight and showed flashes of competence (the 39 nm kill on PushMaster in Round 7) but died four times and recorded a structural G exceedance of 10.83 G in the final slot that demands immediate attention from the maintenance authority. Formation discipline was universally poor — no pilot maintained meaningful formation during BVR, with Golden_Pilot recording a 323 s rejoin time in one slot and ToRnAdO's early-round discipline scores near zero. The blue team won the BVR series 3-1, but margin of victory was narrow and both teams left significant Pk on the table through long-range launches. The recurring theme across all four pilots is trigger discipline and G discipline — both require immediate corrective focus before the next live weapons sortie.
  • G discipline is a life-and-death issue, not a score metric: MeGaTron recorded 9.93 G and 4 ft minAGL; ToRnAdO hit 10.83 G — both pilots must complete an immediate G-awareness ground school and review OBOGS/G-suit serviceability before flying again. There is no kill worth a structural failure at 2,000 ft AGL.
  • BVR trigger discipline: the red team averaged launches at 15–40 nm with sub-10% Pk; blue team closed to 7–12 nm before firing and achieved splashes. The lesson is simple — hold fire until the geometry gives you a sub-1,000 m CPA probability, not when the radar first goes active.
  • Formation standards exist in BVR too: a 2-ship that spends most of a 5-minute engagement with the wingman 7,800 m out of position (Golden_Pilot slot 5) is a 1-ship — the second aircraft provides no mutual support, no target separation, and no tactical flexibility. All pilots must practise the rejoin to within 30 s or the formation authority is degraded.

Megatron

58 pts
bfm_wins 30 · bfm_losses_penalty 0 · bfm_deck_busts_penalty -25 · bvr_kills 12 · bvr_deaths_penalty -24 · over_g_sustained_penalty -20 · airmanship_base 20 · formation_discipline 5 · energy_management 3 · bvr_shot_efficiency 5 · raw_capped 6
+ BFM dominant throughout solo engagements: won Rounds 1, 3, and 4/5 via guns with 12+ hits on PushMaster in Round 4 (saddle time 22 s in Round 4, 7 s in Round 3), demonstrating consistent conversion from neutral to offensive.
+ BVR Round 7: scored a kill on Golden_Pilot at 7.2 nm CPA 36 m — excellent close-in shot discipline when he closed to valid parameters.
− Catastrophic over-G habit: 14 sustained over-G events in the longest BFM slot and 7 in Round 3 slot, with peak recorded G of 9.93 and minAGL as low as 4 ft — this pilot is a single sortie away from a structural failure or CFIT fatality.
− BVR missile employment undisciplined: fired 3 shots from 20.4 nm, 10.8 nm, and 15.9 nm in Round 6 for zero kills, and from 55.7 nm in Round 10 for zero kills — consistently launching outside effective parameters; must study kinematics and Pk curves before next BVR sortie.
Airmanship: MinAGL of 4 ft recorded across slots — this is a ground-strike event waiting to happen. 14 sustained over-G in a single slot at low altitude is professionally unacceptable. No formation data recorded (solo BFM slots), so formation discipline cannot be graded there. Trend is improving from history (32→70→now 58 net) but the G-loading pattern has worsened.

70 pts
bfm_wins 0 · bfm_losses_penalty -8 · bfm_deck_busts_penalty -20 · bvr_kills 48 · bvr_deaths_penalty -18 · over_g_sustained_penalty -4 · airmanship_base 20 · formation_discipline 2 · energy_management 2 · bvr_shot_efficiency 8 · raw_total 70
+ BVR top scorer this session: 5 confirmed kills across Rounds 6, 7, 8, 9, and 10 — including a tight 9.8 nm splash on MeGaTron in Round 6 (CPA 16 m) and a close-in 2.1 nm splash on ToRnAdO in Round 8 (CPA 188 m), demonstrating willingness to hold fire until parameters are valid.
+ BVR shot efficiency: 4 shots per round with multiple splashes, averaged better Pk than either red pilot; consistently defeated all 4 inbound missiles in Round 6 without being struck.
− BFM performance was poor: 3 deck busts in the Round 3 slot (minAGL 131 ft), spent 53% of fight on defence against MeGaTron, energy-poor 6 s at 2,114 ft — needs to practise energy-to-turn-rate management at the merge instead of immediately going defensive.
− Formation discipline critically deficient in BVR: formationDisciplineScore of 0–14 across slots, worst rejoin 323 s (over 5 minutes out of position), avgJoinSec of 97–323 s — a standard requires rejoining within 30 s; this pilot was chronically non-standard.
Airmanship: Over-G was moderate (0–2 sustained events per slot, max 9.2 G). Formation data across BVR slots shows dominant 'spread/none' with discipline scores near zero. The 323 s worst-rejoin time in Round 8 slot is operationally unacceptable for a 2-ship fight — that is the entire engagement duration spent out of position. Energy management flagged as poor in BFM (22 s at 247 kts). Positive: no sustained over-G in final BVR slots.

+ BVR Round 7: scored a clean kill on PushMaster at 39 nm with CPA 117 m — one of the longest-range kills of the session, demonstrating understanding of high-aspect intercept geometry.
+ Formation performance in Rounds 8 and 10 showed improvement: best rejoin times of 3–5 s in slot 3 and slot 4, and maintained wedge/spread formation 56–79% of time in those slots — a measurable step forward from early rounds.
− Died in 4 of 5 BVR slots — the highest death count of the session; primary cause was being struck by missiles he had inbound but did not defeat, combined with launching from excessive range (average launch 26–40 nm) for near-zero Pk results across 11 total shots.
− Over-G is alarming: 5 sustained over-G events in Round 3 slot, 10.1 G recorded in Round 8 slot — a structural exceedance that demands a maintenance inspection and an immediate ground debrief on GLOC recognition and G-warm-up procedures.
Airmanship: MaxG 10.83 G recorded in final slot — this is a hard structural exceedance on the F-16 (limit 9.0 G clean). ToRnAdO's formation discipline improved across the sortie (score 4–25 in later slots vs near-zero early), and rejoin times tightened from 70 s worst to 9 s worst in later slots, showing real learning. However the G issue overrides that positive trend. No BFM data (did not participate in BFM phase). Shot efficiency poor: 11 shots, 1 kill, average launch 30+ nm. Previous history shows trend improving (0→70) but this sortie does not continue that trajectory.
